lead: three trades finished outright, the tools sold each time — and a woman in a town you left in your twenties still rings when the drawer sticks, and you still drive out and plane it true.
sun: you were at the top of the work in the last year of each, and the final thing you made in that line was among the best — which is why nobody believed the announcement. then the bench was sold to a man with a van, and the trade was never practised afterwards in any form, not as a weekend habit and not as a favour. the hands crossed into something else entirely, unharmed.
moon: your hands let go of everything they finished, at the moment they finished it, uncounted, into houses you have no current address for — and each object took a promise with it that the trade's ending did not touch. so the work is gone and the maintenance is not. you owe a hinge, a wobble, a joint you know you rushed.
pull: you have finished three trades and you are still the only person alive who can service the first one. the work ended. the guarantee did not.
tension: wasted is the word, and it is said kindly, usually by somebody holding a thing you made. they have the object in their hands and the memory of you spending a saturday putting it right, and no account you give of the leaving weighs anything against that — someone who has genuinely stopped does not do that. so the offers keep arriving, and every repair you carry out is read as proof that the leaving was never real.
cost: the work stops at the standard you set — no long decline, no bitter late period. and you have kept none of it. no shelf, no photographs, nothing on a wall, because keeping was never part of the making, and the only full account of what your hands could do is scattered across four counties, in houses you enter by appointment, to fix something.

lead: the flat was empty by sunday and nothing in it was argued over. six years later a standing order in your name is still paying for a thing in a house you cannot enter.
sun: everything that was furniture of that life stays where the life was — the flat, the pictures, the good chairs, nine years of a record of what you liked — and none of it gets divided, because dividing assumes a portion is still coming with you. no portion comes. you go out with a bag and a phone, and nothing that was in the rooms follows.
moon: nothing you own has ever been guarded, and it was never a policy — the instinct is simply not in you. what you have is on display inside ten minutes: the shelves, the wrist, the room, priceable by anyone. so at the end there was no hidden half to fall to you, no account nobody knew about. the whole estate was visible, and the whole of it stayed.
pull: nothing you have ever owned was defended. both households kept the lot, with your blessing, and a piano you will never play is still tuned every spring out of your account.
tension: everyone close to you has a version of what you ought to have kept. the settlement is on the record and it reads exactly like a person being taken apart — no valuation, no inventory, no lawyer on either side. the true account, that the contents belonged to a life that ended and you wanted none of them, lands as the story people tell afterwards to feel better about a loss. the tuning bill settles it.
cost: the people you left kept whole houses rather than halves, and each ending went through in a weekend, priced by nobody. what you have now would fit in a car. every life is furnished by somebody else's taste and ends the same way, so no object anywhere holds a decade of you, and the things that could have proved any of it are all in rooms that kept them.

lead: the form asks for two people who have known you five years. you have four lives behind you and neither of the names you finally wrote could say what you do, where you live, or who else knows you.
sun: there was never a body of people in it to lose. you belonged to no trade and appeared on no list, and the colleagues who could have dated the years for you were only ever people in the same building. so each ending took the population of a life and found nothing underneath. a leaving needs no procedure here: one week you are in the town, the following one you are not.
moon: in the towns themselves you were never placed. you are in the room and not of it, and not from concealment — the position never came with a membership. so the endings are not departures from anything; they are the identical standing at a different address. what does hold runs one name at a time: him, her, the woman in the second life who is still owed.
pull: the only people who can place you are the ones you owe. four lives ended, and none of them holds a witness who could describe an ordinary week of yours.
tension: somebody needs you accounted for — a landlord, a hearing, a new person's careful parents — and the only people who can speak for you are the ones you have kept turning up for. their evidence has one item in it: that you turn up. nobody can add what you are like at dinner, or over ten years, or in company, so what gets assembled is a single reliable act with no person around it.
cost: an ending here needs nobody's clearance, and it arrives without a meeting or a notice period. four lives have gone down and left the public record exactly as they found it. what you have instead is a handful of people who each know one true thing about you, and they do not know each other, so the whole of you has never been assembled, including by you.

lead: you resigned on a wednesday and were not at another meeting after it, which is how everything ends with you. the argument itself did not end. it never had one end available to be let go of.
sun: by the friday you were as done with it as a person can be. the side went, the meetings, the mailing list, the people who had been your people for a decade, the standing you had in it — no consultancy afterwards, no advisory role, no quiet word with the ones still inside. by monday there was nothing of the machinery left in your week at all.
moon: the grip is what did not leave. you held both cases from the beginning — theirs at full strength, yours at full strength, no ranking between them, which is the only reason you were any good in it. the leaving removed you from one side of the table and from neither argument. so the whole thing still runs at pressure, both directions, with no room left to run it in.
pull: you ended the fight and kept the grip. both cases are still in you at full weight, and the one person who could argue either of them with you is on the other side.
tension: the ones you left with cannot square a clean break with the call you still take from him every few months, and file it as a line kept warm. the ones you left file the same call as sentiment. the true version needs them to accept that finishing with the whole of it and owing one man a particular thing are unrelated events, and neither side has managed to hold those two apart.
cost: you can walk out of a fight you are winning without taking a faction with you — no splinter group, no grievance running for years under your name, nothing of it operating. the argument keeps its full weight and loses its room. you hold both halves of a thing with no table left, and the two people who could sit with either half will not sit with each other.
